intent: Kept: 5 sensors at x = -0.06 to +0.06 with y = 0.03, 16 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, body_width 0.12. Changed: mass from 0.7 back to 0.8 kg and body_length from 0.14 back to 0.18 m, to restore the iteration-1 inertia after slalom line loss reached 0.85. Expected result: slalom line loss falls to about 0.1 or below and oval stays near 0, with max_error still near 0.063 m. Considering, not committed: wheel_track 0.10 next if line loss is low but max_error stays at about 0.063 m.
learning: Iteration 4 showed slalom line loss of 0.85 with lower inertia and y 0.03, so inertia may be the cause of slalom line loss rather than sensor y alone. This race tests the inertia revert with y held at 0.03. If slalom line loss stays at 0.2 or higher, the controller's kd is the likely cause and geometry should be held.
rationale: Iteration 4 (y 0.03, mass 0.7, body_length 0.14, ±0.06 m span, 16 mm footprints) scored 124.20, the best so far. Oval line loss was 0 and s-bend 0.15, but slalom line loss was 0.85 per run. The Integrator's stated rule says to revert mass to 0.8 and body_length to 0.18 if oval or slalom line loss is 0.2 or higher, and the slalom figure is well above that. Iteration 1 used these values with y 0.03 and had slalom line loss of 0.1. I am therefore taking the Integrator's advice and reverting mass and body_length, keeping sensor y at 0.03, the ±0.06 m span, 16 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.12 and wheel_radius 0.03. Iteration 2 showed that the sensor y 0.02 change raised line loss, so y stays at 0.03. The main cost is likely less s-bend progress, because the lower inertia from iteration 4 helped there (0.39 against 0.14 in iteration 1). I expect slalom line loss near 0.1 and a score in the 112 to 120 range. The best score so far (124) came from the lower-inertia design, so this revert is a trade-off, and I am making it because the rule is explicit and line loss is the more controllable failure. Other Integrator feedback is not yet in view for this design, so I am not changing the controller side.
